doc.title: Konitz Lee — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Gerry Wald's band, Lester Young and the Basie band at the Regal
summary: He played third alto with Gerry Wald, a tenor player introduced him to Lester Young records, and he saw Basie at the Regal.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I read at some point you played with Gerry Wald?
Gerry Wald, in the mid-forties, for a short period.
Yeah. Third alto. Good band. Gerry Wald was a fine clarinet player.
Kind of an Artie Shaw wannabe, right?
Yeah. I don’t think I ever played a solo in that band. But there was a fine tenor player who kind of introduced me to Lester Young, officially by, you know, in

the room getting stoned and all that kind of stuff, listening. I said wow, look at that. Because I’m sure we talked about it with Tristano but, somehow, that was another big impression. Probably heard some different tunes and things like that.
Did you hear the Basie records?
Yeah, but maybe some others ones too, the Basie ones were the first ones I heard. I even heard and saw the Basie band at the, what was the name of the black theater in Chicago?
Regal. I remember this guy with the tenor sideways and everything but I didn’t really know the significance of that yet. I knew it sounded nice but [it wasn’t] until later I found out who it was.
